Subject: Re: Fwd: Service spike + failed requests during morning window (us-west-2) — SRE findings

Vivek/Laura — summary of SRE findings from our initial analysis for us-west-2: 

1) Confirmed disruption window (Redwood-observed): 2026-11-28T18:05:55Z — 2026-11-28T18:12:10Z (06:05:55–06:12:10 UTC) which corresponds to ~10:05:55–10:12:10 PST recorded on Acme's timeline.

2) Cause: a bug in the region autoscaler reconciliation loop triggered a simultaneous scale-down/scale-up cycle under a specific concurrent-connection pattern. During the reconciliation there was a short period where the front-door routing table returned 502/503 for in-flight requests as workers were cycled. We also saw a small surge in retry traffic that amplified tail-latency.

3) Impact scope: ~6m15s of elevated error rate concentrated on a subset of hosts in us-west-2. Total failed requests attributable to the event: 58 (matches customer's CSV within margin).

4) Eligibility: Per Section 3.2 of the SLA, "Unavailable" is defined as when Redwood's service is unable to respond to valid requests. Given the confirmed error spike and duration, Acme meets the threshold for an SLA credit for that window. We recommend triggering a remediation credit evaluation and issuing a pro-rata credit for the affected minute range.

5) Evidence & artifacts (attached): redwood-sre-diagnostics-20261128.txt (router logs snippet), acme_request_logs_20261128.tar.gz (pulled per customer request; redacted), link to the incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7123

Next steps (short term):
- Ops will open a dedicated postmortem and remediation ticket (INF-7123) and assign owners.
- I will prepare a short postmortem draft and timeline; ETA 72 hours for initial RCA.
- Vivek/Laura: recommend we confirm eligibility to Acme and offer the standard SLA credit; keep them apprised of the postmortem ETA.

Attachments: redwood-sre-diagnostics-20261128.txt, acme_request_logs_20261128.tar.gz

— Chloe
